findings.where: The whole tile: the hero mark, the nav lockup 'MMM INFRA' and the palette
findings.fault: The logo appears only as a version the client does not hold. The arches are recoloured from the logo grey #404040 to the near-black 'cut' #2A2925, and the wordmark loses its blue #0070C0. The palette has no place for either logo colour. The granite ground #B8B5AD is too close in lightness to the logo blue for the full-colour logo to sit on it, so on this ground the real logo can never appear.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose logo 'stays' (value 7) and whose blue-and-grey wordmark is the one fixed thing in his identity. The founder, because the house rule is to change the ground or the version, never the logo's colours, and a new version needs the client's yes.

findings.where: The whole tile: no photograph or video slot anywhere, from the first screen to the motion sketch
findings.fault: The tile never shows how Mark himself, or a film, sits on this stone ground. The first screen has the mark and his name set in red capitals, but no face. Nothing tests how a photograph or a video frame looks against flat mid-grey, hard-edged minium and the dark line borders.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who must judge every direction against 'the man himself' (value 3) and 'video welcome' (value 8) and cannot do so here. A development-bank officer on a first visit, who expects to see the named person behind a solo practice before writing to him.

findings.where: The minium red: the hero name, the article title, 'CINZEL', 'LAID · WEIGHTY · SETTLED', and the 'WRITE TO MARK' button
findings.fault: The one accent goes to every heading as well as to the one action. The direction promised 'one accent only, and it flows to the action'. Instead the two-line red name in the hero outweighs the button below it, and on an article page the red title will compete with any red action.
findings.who_objects: A visitor deciding whether to get in touch: the action's colour no longer marks the action, so the button is just one more red thing. The founder, because the direction card's own rule is broken and the primary action's colour is reserved.

findings.where: The pull quote in the article specimen, against the 'WRITE TO MARK' button
findings.fault: The pull quote, which is static, uses the same tabula ansata shape (a framed panel with dovetail handles) as the only button. One shape means two things on the same site. On a phone the quote's large dark handles make a boxed, button-like block in the middle of the article.
findings.who_objects: An article reader, who may tap the quote expecting it to act. Angélique, who will repeat this shape in every post she adds.

findings.where: The 'WRITE TO MARK' button in the first screen; the page has no footer
findings.fault: The only contact route is a mailto button. Mark's email address is never shown as text, and no footer carries it.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer on a locked-down work machine with no mail client set up: the click does nothing, and there is no address to copy into their own mail.

findings.where: The ground of the whole page, including the article specimen
findings.fault: Every part of the site sits on one flat mid-grey with no second surface. Long article text, photographs and PDF thumbnails will all sit on a dim, overcast ground, and the stone the direction promises never appears outside the labelled stand-in.
findings.who_objects: Readers of Mark's articles (Read mode), who get a long text on a grey that reads like a greyed-out page. Mark, whose own grounds were white, a muted colour, blueprint or a legal pad, none of them a dull mid-grey.

findings.where: The article title 'THE WORLD'S BEST PUBLIC-PRIVATE PARTNERSHIP LAW' and the type-pair rule 'Headings … always in capitals, always tracked'
findings.fault: Every heading must be set in tracked Cinzel capitals, so a long post title becomes a three-line block of capitals on a phone and is slow to read. Mark's article titles run long ('Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the 'Abundance' Challenge').
findings.who_objects: Angélique, adding posts with real titles, and the readers who scan a list of articles by title.

findings.where: Type rules the tile sets itself: the byline 'MMM INFRA BLOG NO. 8 · 18 SEPTEMBER 2024', the motion table's headers, and the spacing of words in the article title and hero
findings.fault: The tile breaks its own type rule. It says only headings, the nav and the button take tracked capitals, yet the byline and the table headers take them too. It says words are 'parted by interpuncts', yet the article title uses plain spaces, and the hero puts interpuncts in some places and not others ('MARK · M · MOSELEY' but no interpunct before 'INFRASTRUCTURE'). In 'MARK · M · MOSELEY' the lone middle initial reads as a word of its own.
findings.who_objects: The layout round's designer and Angélique, who cannot tell from the tile which rule to follow.

findings.fault: This is a button, but it is drawn with an underline, the link's mark, and it does not use the tile's own button treatment (the minium tablet).
findings.who_objects: A visitor who reads the underline as a link to another page, and the layout round's designer, who would carry two button looks forward.

findings.fault: The code and the file path fall back to the browser's default monospace font. It sets larger and heavier than the small Alegreya Sans around it, which breaks the colour of the paragraph and lets the default font stack into the tile.
findings.who_objects: The founder, judging the type pair: this is the default font stack the guardrails ban as a voice.
